title: Collisions
body:
A **collision** is a brief interaction where the forces between two objects are much larger
than anything external, so [[Linear Momentum]] is conserved for the pair. Whether
[[Kinetic Energy]] is also conserved is what classifies the collision.

```
perfectly inelastic   objects stick together, maximum energy lost
inelastic             objects separate, some energy lost
elastic               kinetic energy conserved as well as momentum
```

**Perfectly inelastic**, worked:

```
2 kg at 3 m/s strikes 1 kg at rest and they stick together

  momentum:  (2)(3) + (1)(0) = 6 = (3)v      ->  v = 2 m/s

  KE before: ½(2)(3²) = 9 J
  KE after:  ½(3)(2²) = 6 J                  ->  3 J lost
```

Momentum balances exactly and energy does not. The missing 3 J went into deformation, sound and
heat, which is what inelastic means physically. Nothing was violated, since energy conservation
applies to all forms of energy and the mechanical account is only part of it.

**Elastic** collisions conserve both, giving two equations for two unknown final velocities.
Between equal masses with one initially at rest, the solution is that the velocities are
exchanged completely, with the moving object stopping dead and the stationary one leaving at
the original speed. That result is what an air-track demonstration shows and what a Newton's
cradle repeats.

Real collisions between solid objects are close to elastic and never exactly so, which the
laboratory measures by comparing kinetic energy before and after.
